findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The handwashing sink in the dish room needs to be re-sealed to the wall. 
2. There is missing coving to the left of the dish machine. Ensure that this coving is replaced. 

Discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a spoon present in the basin of the hand washing sink. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the spoon to be taken to the dish room. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for handwashing only to incentivize frequent hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed light entering the facility through the back kitchen door (along the bottom perimeter). Discussed this area as a point of potential entry for pests with the PIC. Replace weather stripping by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: No temperature measurement device for heat sanitation was available during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that a new heat dish puck has been ordered, and delayed in shipping. Ensure a heat measuring device for sanitation is made available by 02/06/26 to ensure proper heat sanitation temperatures in a verifiable manner.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the caulk behind the dish-line sprayer to be soiled. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that caulk is either cleaned or replaced.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed tubs of mayonnaise in both the walk-in cooler and prep cooler to have no lids. Discussed with PIC and PIC had them covered immediately. Ensure tubs of mayonnaise not currently in use are covered to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Multiple containers of food in the walk-in cooler and bottom prep cooler were observed to held past the 7 day maximum.  Discussed with PIC, who discarded all items.  Ensure foods are discarded after the 7 day maximum hold time.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
The ice scoop in the ice machine was observed to be laying in the ice with the handle touching the ice.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure the ice scoops are stored outside of the ice machine, or in the ice with the handle up and out of the ice to prevent contamination.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
The coat rack in the kitchen was observed to be touching a shelf holding clean dishes.  There is also a dish apron hanging on a shelf in the dish room that holds clean dishes.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure personal clothing items and aprons are not stored next to clean food contact surfaces to prevent contamination.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket measured 0 ppm (q) during inspection.  While investigating the sanitizer dispenser, it was discovered that the dispenser is malfunctioning.  Employees are going to manually mix the sanitizer until the dispenser is fixed.  Ensure sanitizer concentration is checked regularly in order to properly sanitizer food contact surfaces.  Inspector will spot check for the dispenser in a week.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)
